fullPassage: [P01] A young child may have many experiences with an apple—such as eating it, feeling that it is round, and seeing that it is green or red—long before being asked to label it with the word apple. Music should follow this same pattern of learning. In other words, the child should have experiences with sounds by singing, playing instruments, listening to fast and slow tempos, or loud and soft dynamics before being asked to speak about these labels (fast or slow, loud or soft). Because music is the most abstract of all the arts—that is, it passes through time and exists only in the memory—actual experiences with musical sounds are essential before explaining any specific musical concept. [P02] The success and vigor of scientific research, and the effectiveness of its technological application, are generally accepted as indicators of the quality of a nation's life. Science is so important, and expensive, that the major policy decisions concerning its development are increasingly being taken by the State, rather than being left to the judgment of the scientists and their private patrons. Accordingly, the progress of science becomes a matter of politics; everyone in the community is involved in the consequences of decisions on 'science policy,' and every citizen is responsible, however indirectly, for the formation of those decisions. This social involvement of science will necessarily increase over the decades to come. An increasing number of practical problems will need to be solved through planned programs of scientific and technological research, and the rising cost of the many-sided work of science will call for the most direct involvement of the State in its planning. [P03] Whether a negotiator's goal is a contract or a relationship, the negotiated transactions in almost all cases will be embodied in some sort of written agreement. Cultural factors influence the form of the written agreement that the parties make. Generally, Americans prefer very detailed contracts that attempt to anticipate all possible circumstances and eventualities, no matter how unlikely. Why? Because the deal is the contract itself, and one must refer to the contract to handle new situations that may arise. Other cultures, such as the Chinese, prefer a contract in the form of general principles rather than detailed rules. Why? Because it is claimed that the essence of the deal is the relationship between the parties. If unexpected circumstances arise, the parties should look to their relationship, not the contract, to solve the problem. So, in some cases, a Chinese negotiator may interpret the American drive to specify all possibilities as evidence of a lack of confidence in the stability of the underlying relationship. [P04] In an experiment conducted in the early 1960s, subjects were led to believe that they were participating in a study about the effects of a "vitamin injection." In truth, the injection they received was a small dose of epinephrine, a drug that stimulates the nervous system and produces a degree of physiological arousal. Half the subjects in one condition of the experiment were told that the "vitamins" would lead to an increased heart rate, flushed face, and slight trembling; while in another condition the other half of the volunteers were given no information at all about side effects. The result? When placed in a room with a very happy person, the subjects with no explanation of the drug's effects reported that they were also feeling playful and positive. When placed in a room with an angry person, the uninformed subjects reported feeling hostile and negative. But if subjects knew that their arousal was the result of the injection, their mood remained unchanged by the reactions of those around them.

(B) After four years of hard study, she finally earned a <u>degree</u> in chemistry at the university.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 degree의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) a certain degree of arousal = 어느 '정도'의 각성(명사, 양·수준), (B) earned a degree in chemistry = 화학 '학위'를 받다 ← 정답
❌ ② (A)는 학위가 아니라 '정도'
❌ ③ (A)는 각도가 아니라 '정도'
❌ ④ (B)는 각도가 아니라 '학위'
det.tip: degree는 '정도·수준', '학위', '(온도·각도의) 도' 등 여러 뜻을 가집니다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who gives money or support to a person, organization, or activity"

det.analysis:
❌ ① negotiator: 협상가
❌ ② volunteer: 자원봉사자
✅ ③ patron: 사람·단체·활동에 돈이나 지원을 제공하는 '후원자' ← 정답
❌ ④ subject: (실험) 대상자
det.tip: 돈이나 지원을 대 주는 사람 = patron(후원자). 본문 their private patrons 참고

questions.passage: Whether a negotiator's goal is a contract or a relationship, the negotiated transactions in almost all cases will be __________ (embody) in some sort of written agreement.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: will be ___ 는 '~에 담길 것이다'라는 미래 수동태(will be + 과거분사)이다. embody의 과거분사는 embodied이므로 will be embodied가 맞다.
det.tip: 수동태 be + p.p.: will be embodied(담기게 될 것이다)

questions.passage: __________ (place) in a room with a very happy person, the subjects with no explanation of the drug's effects reported that they were also feeling playful and positive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 콤마 앞부분은 주어 the subjects를 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문이다. 피험자들이 방에 '놓이는' 것은 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 Placed로 시작하는 분사구문(= When they were placed ~)이 맞다.
det.tip: 수동 분사구문은 과거분사로 시작: Placed in a room ~, the subjects reported ~

questions.passage: [P01] A young child may have many experiences with an apple—such as eating it, feeling that it is round, and seeing that it is green or red—long before being asked to label it with the word apple. Music should follow this same pattern of learning. In other words, the child should have experiences with sounds by singing, playing instruments, listening to fast and slow tempos, or loud and soft dynamics before being asked to speak about these labels (fast or slow, loud or soft). Because music is the most abstract of all the arts—that is, it passes through time and exists only in the memory—actual experiences with musical sounds are essential before explaining any specific musical concept. [P02] The success and vigor of scientific research, and the effectiveness of its technological application, are generally accepted as indicators of the quality of a nation's life. Science is so important, and expensive, that the major policy decisions concerning its development are increasingly being taken by the State, rather than being left to the judgment of the scientists and their private patrons. Accordingly, the progress of science becomes a matter of politics; everyone in the community is involved in the consequences of decisions on 'science policy,' and every citizen is responsible, however indirectly, for the formation of those decisions. This social involvement of science will necessarily increase over the decades to come. An increasing number of practical problems will need to be solved through planned programs of scientific and technological research, and the rising cost of the many-sided work of science will call for the most direct involvement of the State in its planning. [P03] Whether a negotiator's goal is a contract or a relationship, the negotiated transactions in almost all cases will be embodied in some sort of written agreement. Cultural factors influence the form of the written agreement that the parties make. Generally, Americans prefer very detailed contracts that attempt to anticipate all possible circumstances and eventualities, __________ unlikely. Why? Because the deal is the contract itself, and one must refer to the contract to handle new situations that may arise. Other cultures, such as the Chinese, prefer a contract in the form of general principles rather than detailed rules. Why? Because it is claimed that the essence of the deal is the relationship between the parties. If unexpected circumstances arise, the parties should look to their relationship, not the contract, to solve the problem. So, in some cases, a Chinese negotiator may interpret the American drive to specify all possibilities as evidence of a lack of confidence in the stability of the underlying relationship. [P04] In an experiment conducted in the early 1960s, subjects were led to believe that they were participating in a study about the effects of a "vitamin injection." In truth, the injection they received was a small dose of epinephrine, a drug that stimulates the nervous system and produces a degree of physiological arousal. Half the subjects in one condition of the experiment were told that the "vitamins" would lead to an increased heart rate, flushed face, and slight trembling; while in another condition the other half of the volunteers were given no information at all about side effects. The result? When placed in a room with a very happy person, the subjects with no explanation of the drug's effects reported that they were also feeling playful and positive. When placed in a room with an angry person, the uninformed subjects reported feeling hostile and negative. But if subjects knew that their arousal was the result of the injection, their mood remained unchanged by the reactions of those around them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① as long as(~하는 한): 문맥상 어색함
✅ ② no matter how(아무리 ~해도): 모든 상황과 가능성을 '아무리 가능성이 낮더라도' 예상하려 한다는 양보의 의미 ← 정답
❌ ③ in order to(~하기 위해): 뒤에 형용사 unlikely와 연결 불가
❌ ④ rather than(~보다는): 대조 의미로 문맥에 맞지 않음
det.tip: all possible circumstances ~, __________ unlikely → 아무리 가능성이 낮아도(no matter how)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① led to believe(믿도록 유도되다): 피험자들이 '비타민 주사' 연구에 참여한다고 '믿도록 유도되었다'는 실험 조작 상황 ← 정답
❌ ② forced to deny(부인하도록 강요받다): 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ asked to prove(증명하도록 요청받다): 문맥상 어색함
❌ ④ allowed to reject(거부하도록 허용되다): 문맥상 어색함
det.tip: subjects were __________ that they were participating ~ → 믿도록 유도되다(led to believe)
